## Frequently Asked Questions


###### Is the "free plan" really free?


Yes. You can get started with our free plan at zero cost. The starter plan gives you access to all Tenjin features including cost aggregation, ad revenue LTV, and up to 2,000 free conversions per month.


###### How do I upgrade to a different plan?


Super easy, you can upgrade to a different plan at any time by simply sending an email to support@tenjin.com.


###### How do you charge for the SKAdNetwork/iOS14 solution?


It’s free! All Tenjin customers get access to our SKAdNetwork solution. With the evolving SKAdNetwork framework, it’s been one of our first priorities to make sure our customers can utilize this data effectively.


###### What are the payment options?


We accept all major credit cards, direct debit and bank wire transfer.


###### What is a conversion?


Tenjin counts a conversion when a user installs your mobile app after clicking on an ad. In other words, conversions in Tenjin reflect installs driven by paid marketing or user acquisition campaigns. Installs from organic sources, like ASO, are not considered conversions. Tenjin does not limit or charge for organic installs.

###### TENJIN MMP


# Tenjin: The Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) for Growth


Certified by all the marketing channels you need, Tenjin empowers growing mobile publishers to scale with simple yet effective advertising measurement tools.


[Free sign up](<https://dashboard.tenjin.com/signup>) [Book a demo](<https://tenjin.com/mmp/#book-demo>)


###### Powering Mobile Publishers Around the World


#### Invest in a MMP you can trust


Accurate attribution and reliable data are essential for mobile marketing success. As a certified partner of Meta, TikTok, and Google, Tenjin provides trusted measurement to help users optimize their mobile marketing campaigns with confidence.


#### Enjoy a seamless integration with any Partner


Tenjin is integrated with 1000+ [integrated partners](<https://tenjin.com/partners/>). Don’t see the partner you need? Use our ‘Custom Channels’ option or connect with our Partnership team to easily set up campaigns for networks we haven’t integrated with yet.


###### Growth-friendly, all-inclusive pricing


Tenjin empowers mobile publishers to scale their apps with ease. Our [transparent pricing](<https://tenjin.com/pricing/>)includes all add-ons—such as ROAS campaigns—across every plan, eliminating hidden costs so teams can focus entirely on growth.


###### Experience an user-friendly dashboard


Tenjin’s intuitive, user-friendly dashboard is designed to be easy to learn, even for teams using an MMP for the first time. With clear, intuitive reports and real-time insights, your team can quickly navigate the platform.


###### Get fast & reliable support for growing teams


Tenjin is built for growing teams, providing dedicated support to simplify mobile attribution. From seamless integration to quick issue resolution and expert guidance, we take care of the details—so you can focus on scaling your business.


### Customer Success Stories


#### Kooapps' journey from from indie studio to major publisher with Tenjin


In this case study, we take you through the journey of Kooapps as they scale from an indie studio to a major publisher with Tenjin. Here is a summary of the results they achieved using Tenjin’s ad attribution, session-based ad revenue LTV, and DataVault:


- 8x Revenue Growth

- 3x LTV increase


[Image: CK Wang - Kooapps CEO]   Chun-Kai WangCo-founder & CEO at Kooapps


Revenue is up 8x since we first used Tenjin a few years ago and paid UA spend is 30x so Tenjin has completely transformed our business. We love Tenjin!


[Read More](<https://tenjin.com/blog/how-to-scale-your-indie-studio-to-a-major-publisher/%20>)


#### How Mexico’s Top Mobile Publisher Boosted their Portfolio LTV by 35% – A HyperBeard Case Study


HyperBeard is the largest mobile game developer and publisher in Mexico, with 210 Million+ downloads on AppStore and PlayStore. They specialize in cute casual idle games targeting a young, adult, female demographic.


- 20% increase in ROAS

- 35% Portfolio LTV (cross-promo) uplift


[Image: Alex Kozachenko - CEO of HyperBeard]   Alex KozachenkoCo-founder & CEO at HyperBeard


We love using DataVault. Historically, we were just using whatever was available on the dashboard with whatever MMP we were using. But obviously, that’s pretty limited. DataVault allows us to expand beyond the Tenjin dashboard. It’s great for creative performance tracking, and Portfolio LTV analysis.


[Read More](<https://tenjin.com/blog/how-mexicos-top-mobile-publisher-boosted-their-portfolio-ltv-by-35-a-hyperbeard-case-study/%20>)


#### Ad Revenue Callbacks and ROAS campaigns increased YOMI Studio’s ARPDAU by 60% – Case Study


In this case study, we take you through the journey of YOMI Studio as they enter an unprecedented phase of hyper-growth after incorporating Tenjin’s Ad Revenue Callbacks and ROAS Campaigns. Here is a summary of what they achieved:


- 60 hours per month of co-founder’s time saved

- 60% ARPDAU uplift


[Image: Kasuga Yachi Marketing Section Manager at Tokyo Tsushin]   Light NguyenCo-founder at YOMI studio


Combining Tenjin Ad Revenue Callbacks and ROAS campaigns has enabled us to spend less time on optimization but still scale campaigns at will, moving YOMI into an unprecedented phase of hyper-growth.


[Read More](<https://tenjin.com/blog/how-yomi-studio-unlocked-hyper-growth-with-tenjins-ad-revenue-callbacks/>)


#### How to increase ROAS and LTV for SKAN campaigns with TikTok & Tenjin – A Tokyo Tsushin Case Study


Tokyo Tsushin partnered with TikTok and Tenjin to easily identify users who would trigger valuable in-app events such as purchase, subscribe, and level completion, while controlling costs.


- 33% increase in Day 7 ROAS

- 24% increase in Day 3 LTV


[Image: Kasuga Yachi Marketing Section Manager at Tokyo Tsushin]   Kasuga YachiMarketing Section Manager at Tokyo Tsushin


Launching scalable SKAN campaigns is definitely a challenge. Thanks to the combination of TikTok and Tenjin, we were able to run goal-oriented SKAN campaigns at scale.


[Read More](<https://tenjin.com/blog/how-to-increase-roas-and-ltv-for-skan-campaigns-with-tiktok-tenjin/>)


## Learn more about our MMP


- ###### Frequently asked questions


1. [How to start using Tenjin as my MMP?](<https://tenjin.com/mmp/#>)

You can easily [sign up](<https://dashboard.tenjin.com/signup>) to Tenjin. To make onboarding easier, we provide a free plan with 2,000 conversions per month, allowing mobile publishers to explore the platform before committing.

2. [What is a Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP)?](<https://tenjin.com/mmp/#>)

A Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) is an attribution platform that helps mobile app marketers measure, analyze, and optimize their user acquisition campaigns across various advertising channels. MMPs provide a unified dashboard where marketers can see which marketing campaigns drive the most ROI, while ensuring accurate attribution across paid, and organic sources. To learn more on why you need a MMP, how it works, and what the benefits of using it are, check out [this article](<https://docs.tenjin.com/docs/mmp>).

3. [Is Tenjin an official Meta Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP)?](<https://tenjin.com/mmp/#>)

Yes! Tenjin is one of the seven companies in the world to become a Meta MMP. You can see the full list [here](<https://www.facebook.com/business/partner-directory/search?solution_type=measurement&capabilities=Mobile%20Measurement%20Partners%20(MMP)>).
 
 This means Tenjin advertisers can seamlessly measure and optimize their mobile app campaigns across Meta’s platforms, including Facebook and Instagram. [Learn more](<https://tenjin.com/blog/tenjin-meta-mmp/>).

4. [How many partners is Tenjin integrated with?](<https://tenjin.com/mmp/#>)

Tenjin is integrated with 1000+ partners. You can see the full list of Partners in our [“Integrated Partners” Page](<https://tenjin.com/partners/>).

## Learn more about our Ad Monetization Suite


- ###### Frequently asked questions


1. [What’s the difference between the ad monetization suite and ad revenue aggregation / ad revenue attribution reporting?](<https://tenjin.com/ad-monetization-suite/#>)

Our ad monetization suite helps you capture the result of your ad monetization efforts. This includes important metrics such as eCPM, eCPC, and Ad Revenue, that you need access to when you choose to monetize via showing ads in your app.


Our [ad revenue aggregation](<https://tenjin.com/cost-ad-revenue-aggregation/>), alongside your cost aggregation, helps you understand how every dollar you spend contributes to the growth of your business. You can get started with ad spend and ad revenue reporting completely free of cost with Tenjin, without any limitations. No hidden cost, no SDK integration needed. Just [sign up](<https://tenjin.com/signup>) to our dashboard for free.

2. [What is aggregate-based LTV, and how can I use it?](<https://tenjin.com/ad-monetization-suite/#>)

Tenjin’s aggregate-based LTV allows companies to bridge data gaps caused by user-level tracking limitations, and the shift to a more privacy-centric ecosystem. With this type of LTV calculation, companies can extrapolate revenue across all users (instead of using user-level data) and rely on more accurate data, which boosts their confidence in decision-making.


[Here’s](<https://tenjin.com/blog/how-mexicos-top-mobile-publisher-boosted-their-portfolio-ltv-by-35-a-hyperbeard-case-study/>) an example of how our customer’s achieve success using aggregate-based LTV.

3. [How is LTV/ROAS calculated using the aggregate-based LTV method?](<https://tenjin.com/ad-monetization-suite/#>)

Tenjin allocates ad revenue using the session counts from SDK to calculate LTV or ROAS. This total must be somehow distributed and assigned to each user’s source channel. We use the proportion of app sessions generated by the user (on that day, in that app) to estimate how much ad revenue to assign to each source channel.


Check out our documentation for more details, with an included example [here](<https://docs.tenjin.com/docs/attribution-faq#why-are-ltv-roas-on-the-tenjin-dashboard-different-from-the-applovin-dashboard>).

These are the fraud metrics we currently support:


- Blocked clicks : The number of clicks we blocked based on mean time to install (MTTI).

- Fraudulent purchases: The number of purchases marked as fraudulent

- Blocked fraudulent revenue: revenue amount marked as fraudulent

- Total fraud events: sum of blocked clicks and fraudulent purchases

- Site ID or traffic source ID


Learn more about fraud [here](<https://tenjin.com/docs/fraud/>).

4. [Can you tell me exactly how you identify fraud?](<https://tenjin.com/fraud-prevention/#>)

We can’t reveal all of the methods we use because we don’t want fraudsters to know it and adapt accordingly. However, here are some of the most common anti-fraud methods that are included in our suite:


- Anti-click injection: blocks fraud clicks based on mean time to install (MTTI)

- Click & install mismatch detection: blocks installs that are misaligned with attributed clicks based on various factors.

5. [Can you help me build a custom fraud report?](<https://tenjin.com/fraud-prevention/#>)

You can use [DataVault](<https://tenjin.com/marketing-data-warehouse/>) in conjunction with Growth Fullstack to create tailored reports based on your business needs. Reach out to us at [info@growthfullstack.com](<mailto:info@growthfullstack.com>) to learn more about this.

2. [What Is Server-To-Server Tracking?](<https://tenjin.com/s2s-server-to-server-tracking/#>)

[Server-to-Server (S2S) tracking](<https://tenjin.com/docs/server-to-server-s2s-callbacks/>) connects your server directly to Tenjin via API instead of installing an SDK in your app. This gives you complete data ownership, zero app code changes, and powerful attribution analytics without SDK overhead. 3. [What Is Server-To-Server Integration?](<https://tenjin.com/s2s-server-to-server-tracking/#>)

Server-to-Server (S2S) integration is an API-based setup that connects your backend directly to Tenjin for mobile attribution, so no SDK installation is required in your app.

4. [What Is Server-Side Tracking vs S2S Tracking?](<https://tenjin.com/s2s-server-to-server-tracking/#>)

These terms are often used interchangeably in mobile attribution. Server-to-Server (S2S) is a specific type of server-side tracking where data flows directly between servers via API, which is what Tenjin offers.

S2S integration isn’t plug-and-play. ## Learn More About Site ID Optimization


- ###### Frequently Asked Questions


1. [What is a site ID?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

In mobile marketing, a [site ID](<https://tenjin.com/glossary/site-id/>) is a unique identifier for the publisher app, source, or website where an ad appeared. Depending on the ad network, it could also be called a publisher ID or source ID. These are all the same. Analyzing using IDs helps mobile marketers determine which placements are best for their business and which ones could be low-quality or fraudulent traffic.

2. [How does Tenjin’s SIO work?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

Once you choose which site IDs to block, Tenjin stops sending reports to your selected ad networks. By halting callbacks, it prevents all installs from being attributed.

3. [Does SIO stop ads from being shown to users?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

No. SIO prevents selected site IDs from being attributed within Tenjin. It does not stop the ad networks from serving ads. We recommend contacting your network partner when handling potential fraud for wider traffic-quality issues.

4. [Can you block a site ID across every app and campaign?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

Yes. You can apply a block globally or scope it to your parameters of choice: app, channel, or campaign. This makes it easier to remove repeat offenders, while also keeping more targeted rules for isolated issues.

5. [Is SIO the same as automatic fraud detection?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

No. Tenjin has a mobile ad fraud prevention suite with tools to identify and reject certain fraudulent activity. SIO is a separate control for teams conducting their own fraud analysis or campaign optimization. Your team can pinpoint which site IDs should be excluded.

6. [Can I use site ID optimization without an API?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

Yes. you can upload and block site IDs from the Tenjin Dashboard. Just navigate to Configure > Site ID Optimizations. The API remains available for teams that want to automate updates or manage site IDs at a greater scale.

7. [Is site ID optimization included in every Tenjin plan?](<https://tenjin.com/site-id-optimization/#>)

Yes. Site ID optimization and Tenjin’s fraud prevention suite are both included in every all-inclusive free and paid plan, with no separate add-ons.

Key subscription metrics include trial starts, trial-to-paid conversion rate, active subscribers, renewal rate, churn rate, cancellation rate, subscription revenue, customer lifetime value (LTV), and return on ad spend (ROAS).

SECTION 2: SERVICES PRIVACY POLICY


2.1 Our Role


Tenjin provides tools and services to mobile app developers and publishers so that they can track and analyze certain end user actions in the context of mobile marketing. With respect to the Services, Tenjin acts as a data processor (under the GDPR/UK GDPR) or service provider (under the CCPA/CPRA) on behalf of its customers, who are the data controllers (or businesses, as applicable). Tenjin processes information sent by its customers from their mobile apps, websites, servers, and platform integrations. Tenjin does not collect data directly from end users of its customers’ applications and has no direct relationship with them.


2.2 Customer Data


“Customer Data” means advertising campaign data, in-app event data, subscription data, or other information made available to Tenjin by or on behalf of a customer, its authorized users, or via the customer’s use of the Services or Tenjin Tools. We format and otherwise process Customer Data to help our customers understand and analyze the effectiveness of and costs associated with their advertising campaigns, subscription revenue, and user acquisition and re-engagement activities across various channels.


2.3 How We Collect Customer Data


We collect Customer Data through the following mechanisms:


Tenjin SDK: A software development kit that customers integrate into their mobile applications. The SDK collects device and usage data as configured by the customer, including install, session, and custom in-app events.


Server-to-Server (S2S) Integrations: Customers may send the same categories of data from their own servers to the Tenjin API instead of, or in addition to, using the SDK.


Partner Integrations: Customers may connect advertising networks, ad mediation platforms, analytics providers, and other marketing channels to the Tenjin Platform. Through these integrations Tenjin receives campaign performance and cost data as well as ad click, impression, and view data used for attribution, and sends attribution results and event data back to the partners the customer has enabled (for example through postbacks and callbacks).


Customer Credentials: For certain features such as subscription revenue tracking, customers may provide platform credentials (such as App Store Connect keys) to enable Tenjin to retrieve data on the customer’s behalf.


Web-to-App Attribution: For cross-platform attribution, customers may use Tenjin tracking links, landing pages, and deferred deep linking to connect an interaction on a web page to an app install. Customers are responsible for obtaining any consents required on their web properties.


MCP Server and Agent Plugins: Tenjin’s MCP Server is a hosted service that allows an AI assistant authorized by the customer (such as Claude or Codex) to read the customer’s aggregated reporting data and account configuration and to perform account management actions on the customer’s instruction. The MCP Server does not expose end user personal data unless the customer has enabled a data export feature. Tenjin does not send data to any AI assistant on its own initiative and does not control how the customer’s AI assistant processes data it receives.


2.4 Types of End User Data Processed


Customers may send information about individuals using their apps (“End Users”) to Tenjin for processing and storage. This information may include:


Advertising ID (IDFA, Google Ad ID); Vendor ID; the Tenjin analytics installation ID and other pseudonymous device or install identifiers generated by the Tenjin SDK; IP address; device type, model, locale, and country; OS platform and version; bundle ID; app version; SDK version; Limit Ad Tracking / App Tracking Transparency setting; Apple Search attribution data; ad click, impression, and view data received from Partner Integrations; subscription events and transaction metadata (trials, activations, renewals, cancellations, revenue); custom in-app event data; and web-to-app tracking identifiers.


Where a customer has enabled re-engagement or reinstall attribution and the End User has given the required consent, Tenjin stores a pointer linking the advertising ID to the Tenjin analytics installation ID so that a later re-engagement or reinstall can be attributed to the original campaign. The pointer is retained for a maximum of 24 months.


2.5 How We Use Customer Data


We use Customer Data to provide the Services to the relevant customer, including:


- Mobile attribution and install tracking, including re-engagement and reinstall attribution.

- Cost aggregation and ROI measurement.

- Ad revenue measurement and monetization analytics.

- Predictive analytics and lifetime value prediction (pLTV), using machine learning models applied to Customer Data to forecast user revenue potential.

- Fraud detection and prevention, using behavioral pattern analysis to identify invalid traffic and protect advertising spend, including fraud filters configured by the customer. Tenjin also derives fraud signals at the level of advertising channels and placements (not at the level of individual devices) and applies them across the platform for the benefit of all customers.

- Subscription revenue tracking and reporting.

- Data warehousing and export through DataVault, the Raw Data Exporter, the Cloud Data Exporter, and similar features, where enabled by the customer.

- Campaign automation and account management, including through the Tenjin APIs and the MCP Server.

- Transfer of attribution results and event data to the Partner Integrations enabled by the customer.


The predictive analytics and fraud outputs produced by the Services are automated estimates that support our customers’ marketing decisions. They are not used to make decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects on End Users.


We do not share Customer Data with any customer other than the customer to which it relates, unless we have received the prior express written consent of the customer.


2.6 Aggregated and De-Identified Data


Unless prohibited by applicable law or advertising network terms, we may aggregate Customer Data such that it is not reasonably identifiable with the customer or any end user (“Aggregate Data”). We may use Aggregate Data for industry research and analysis, benchmarking, improving our services, training and improving machine learning models, deriving channel-level fraud signals, and other lawful business purposes. We implement appropriate technical safeguards to prevent re-identification of Aggregate Data.


2.7 Disclosure of Customer Data


We may disclose Customer Data:


- To our subprocessors (as listed in our Data Processing Addendum) for the purpose of providing the Services.

- To the Partner Integrations (advertising networks, mediation platforms, analytics providers, and other marketing channels) that the customer enables in their Tenjin account, for the purposes of install and re-engagement attribution, campaign optimization, and analytics, in accordance with the customer’s instructions and the applicable terms. The customer selects these partners and is responsible for the legal basis of each transfer.

- To the AI assistant that the customer has connected to the MCP Server, in response to the requests of that AI assistant and on the customer’s instruction.

- In connection with any reorganization, merger, sale, joint venture, assignment, transfer, or other disposition of all or any portion of our business, assets, or stock.

- Where we believe disclosure is necessary or appropriate under applicable law, to comply with legal process, to respond to governmental authorities, to enforce our terms, or to protect rights, privacy, safety, or property.


2.8 Data Security


Tenjin uses appropriate and reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect data from loss, misuse, and unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, and destruction. Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256). Our infrastructure is hosted on Amazon Web Services in the United States. Further details regarding Tenjin’s security posture, certifications, and controls are available at our Trust Center: https://app.vanta.com/tenjin.com/trust/ywn3l93hj2amywx3h6448.


2.9 Data Retention for the Services


Customer Data is retained for the maximum periods set out in the retention schedule of our Data Processing Addendum. In summary, event-level data is retained for up to 180 days and attribution records and subscription data for up to 24 months from collection. These are maximum periods and data may be deleted sooner. When a customer’s account is closed, we stop collecting new data and delete the remaining Customer Data at the end of the applicable retention period, or earlier on the customer’s request. A downgrade to the free plan does not close the account; Customer Data continues to be retained under the same retention periods.


2.10 Customer and End User Rights


Tenjin processes Customer Data on behalf of its customers. If you are an end user of a Tenjin customer’s mobile app and you wish to exercise your data protection rights (including rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, or objection), you must contact the owner or operator of the mobile app directly, as they are the data controller. Tenjin will assist its customers in responding to data subject requests in accordance with applicable Data Protection Laws and the terms of its Data Processing Addendum.


Tenjin recognizes data subject rights under the GDPR (including the Right to Erasure under Article 17), the UK GDPR, the Swiss FADP, and the CCPA/CPRA. Since Tenjin is a data processor / service provider, requests should be directed to the relevant customer (the data controller / business). If you contact Tenjin directly, we will direct you to the appropriate customer where possible.


SECTION 3: YOUR PRIVACY RIGHTS


3.1 Rights Under the GDPR, UK GDPR, and Swiss FADP


If you are located in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, you have the following rights with respect to personal information we process as a data controller (i.e., information collected through the Websites and in the course of our customer relationships):


Right of Access: You have the right to request a copy of the personal information we hold about you.


Right to Rectification: You have the right to request correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal information.


Right to Erasure: You have the right to request deletion of your personal information in certain circumstances.


Right to Restriction: You have the right to request that we restrict the processing of your personal information in certain circumstances.


Right to Data Portability: You have the right to receive your personal information in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format.


Right to Object: You have the right to object to the processing of your personal information where we rely on legitimate interests as the legal basis, including direct marketing.


Right to Withdraw Consent: Where we rely on consent, you have the right to withdraw consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.


Right to Lodge a Complaint: You have the right to lodge a complaint with us and with a supervisory authority in your jurisdiction.


To exercise these rights, please contact us at privacy@tenjin.com.


3.2 Rights Under the CCPA/CPRA


If you are a California resident, you have the following rights under the CCPA, as amended by the CPRA:


Right to Know: You have the right to request that we disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal information we have collected about you, the categories of sources, the business purposes for collection, and the categories of third parties with whom we share personal information.


Right to Delete: You have the right to request deletion of personal information we have collected from you, subject to certain exceptions.


Right to Correct: You have the right to request correction of inaccurate personal information.


Right to Opt-Out of Sale/Sharing: You have the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information. Tenjin does not sell personal information collected through the Websites. Tenjin does not share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising purposes, other than through the advertising cookies and tags that you can decline in the cookie banner.


Right to Non-Discrimination: You have the right not to be discriminated against for exercising your privacy rights.


To exercise these rights, please contact us at privacy@tenjin.com. We will verify your identity before responding to your request.


3.3 Rights Under Other US State Privacy Laws


If you are a resident of a US state with an applicable comprehensive privacy law (including Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Texas, Oregon, Montana, Utah, Iowa, Delaware, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Nebraska, Tennessee, Minnesota, Maryland, Indiana, Kentucky, and Rhode Island), you may have similar rights to those described above, including rights to access, delete, correct, and opt out of certain processing activities. The specific rights and procedures may vary by state. To exercise your rights, please contact us at privacy@tenjin.com. Where applicable, you may appeal our decision regarding your request by contacting us at the same address.


SECTION 4: GENERAL PROVISIONS


4.1 Children’s Privacy


The Websites are not directed to children under 16 years of age, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 16 through the Websites. With respect to the Services, Tenjin acts as a data processor on behalf of its customers. Customers are responsible for identifying their child-directed apps in their Tenjin account and for complying with COPPA and other applicable children’s privacy laws, including obtaining verifiable parental consent where required and separate consent for any disclosure to third-party partners, before transmitting any data relating to children to Tenjin or enabling partner integrations for such apps.

This Privacy Policy does not address, and we are not responsible for, the privacy practices of any third parties, including the AI assistants that customers connect to the MCP Server. The inclusion of a link on the Websites does not imply endorsement of the linked site or service.


4.3 Do Not Track and Opt-Out Preference Signals


Some browsers include a “Do Not Track” (DNT) feature. Because there is no industry consensus on how to respond to DNT signals, the Websites do not currently respond to DNT signals. You can manage your cookie preferences through the cookie consent banner on the Websites. 3. Processing Terms for Customer Personal Data.

You agree to pay all charges invoiced to You or incurred by users of Your credit card, debit card, or other payment method used in connection with a purchase or transaction or other monetary transaction interaction with Tenjin or the Tenjin Platform.


8.3.2 You shall pay all applicable subscription fees, including any sales, excise, service, use, or other taxes now or hereafter imposed upon or required to be collected by Tenjin by any authority in connection with or arising from the Tenjin Platform and/or this Agreement, excluding taxes based upon Tenjin’s net income. Where applicable, if You choose to pay by credit card or another payment method that incurs processing fees, such fees may be passed on to You.


8.3.3 You shall pay each invoice issued by Tenjin by the applicable due date and in the currency specified by Tenjin. Any amounts not paid when due shall bear interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate allowed by law, whichever is less.


8.4 No Refunds. In the event You cancel Your Subscription (as defined below), You are not guaranteed any refund or exchange for any unused time on a Subscription, any license or Subscription fees for any portion of the Tenjin Platform, any content or data associated with Your account, or for anything else; however, Tenjin reserves the right to provide refunds and exchanges in appropriate circumstances in its sole discretion.


8.5 Fair Usage Policy. Tenjin reserves the right to review and adjust service terms if a Customer’s usage of the Tenjin Platform, the MCP Server, the Tenjin APIs, and/or related services materially exceeds normal or anticipated usage patterns, resulting in excessive costs or service degradation. In such cases, Tenjin may discuss alternative pricing or temporarily suspend access until a resolution is reached.


9. TERM


9.1 Agreement Term. This Agreement is effective unless terminated in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.


9.2 Subscription Term under a Purchase Order. Where You have a Purchase Order, Your subscription to the Tenjin Platform (“Subscription”) shall commence on the subscription start date indicated on the Purchase Order, and unless earlier terminated pursuant to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, shall continue until the subscription end date set forth on the Purchase Order (the “Initial Subscription Term”), except as otherwise provided below. Thereafter, Your Subscription will automatically renew for additional successive terms equal to the period of the Initial Subscription Term (each, a “Renewal Subscription Term;” the Initial Subscription Term together with each Renewal Subscription Term shall be collectively referred to as the “Subscription Term”), unless either party provides the other party with written notice of its intent to prevent the renewal of Your Subscription at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Subscription Term.


9.3 Self-Serve Plans. Where You purchase a Self-Serve Plan, Your Subscription shall commence on the date of purchase and shall continue for successive monthly periods until cancelled. Each monthly period is a Subscription Term for the purposes of this Agreement. You may cancel a Self-Serve Plan at any time through the Tenjin Platform; cancellation takes effect at the end of the then-current monthly period and no notice period applies. Unless You close Your account, cancellation of a Self-Serve Plan returns Your account to the free plan under Section 9.4.


9.4 Free Plan. If You have not registered for a paid Subscription, the Subscription Term shall commence on the date of registration for the Tenjin Platform and continue until the earlier of (a) the termination or expiration of this Agreement or (b) the date You are notified (as provided under this Agreement) that the services to which You have subscribed have become paid services. Upon registration for the paid services, the previous free Subscription Term shall immediately terminate, and a paid Subscription Term shall commence. A downgrade from a paid Subscription to the free plan, whether by cancellation, non-renewal, or expiry of a Purchase Order, is not a termination of this Agreement. Your account, Your Data, and Your configuration remain available under the free plan, subject to the PTI Limit and the retention periods set out in the Data Processing Addendum, and this Agreement continues to apply.


9.5 Upgrade or Downgrade. For Purchase Orders, an upgrade of the chosen package leads to a new start of the current Subscription Term, and a downgrade is only possible from the beginning of the next Subscription Term with at least thirty (30) days’ written notice provided to Tenjin prior to the expiration of the current Subscription Term. For Self-Serve Plans, an upgrade takes effect on the day it is selected in the Tenjin Platform and is charged on a pro rata basis for the remainder of the current monthly period, and a downgrade takes effect from the first day of the next monthly period; no written notice is required.


10. TERMINATION


10.1 Termination. If a party defaults in the performance of any material provision of this Agreement, then the other party may give written notice to the defaulting party that if the default is not cured within thirty (30) days, the Agreement will be automatically terminated. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenjin may immediately terminate this Agreement and the rights granted hereunder in the event of any breach or alleged breach by You or any Authorized User of Sections 3, 5.2, 7.3, 7.4, 7.5, or 7.7 of this Agreement (or any portion thereof), as determined by Tenjin. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary and without limiting the foregoing, Tenjin may permanently or temporarily terminate or suspend Your access to the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool or any portion thereof immediately without liability if: (i) Tenjin suspects that You or any of Your Authorized Users is using the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool in a way that violates this Agreement and/or could expose Tenjin or any other entity to harm or legal liability; (ii) Tenjin in its sole discretion believes it is required to do so by law; (iii) You cancel the contract; (iv) You default on payment or experience other payment issues; or (v) Free users exceed agreed PTI Limits and/or do not provide billing details upon request.


10.2 Effect of Termination.


10.2.1 Upon the effective date of termination of this Agreement or closure of Your account for any reason, whether by You or Tenjin: (i) all licenses granted to You hereunder shall terminate; (ii) Your right to use and access the Tenjin Platform and all Tenjin Tools shall cease; (iii) You shall immediately cease accessing and using the Tenjin Platform and all Tenjin Tools and shall disconnect any AI Assistant from the MCP Server; (iv) Tenjin shall stop collecting new Your Data for Your account; and (v) Tenjin shall delete any Customer Credentials held by Tenjin in connection with this Agreement within thirty (30) days, unless otherwise required by applicable law. For clarity, the expiry of a paid Subscription Term followed by continued use of the free plan is not a termination or closure for the purposes of this Section 10.2. Your Data will be deleted in accordance with the retention schedule set out in the Data Processing Addendum. You may export Your data using the export functionality included in Your Subscription before the effective date of termination; any extraction, format, or delivery beyond that functionality is a separately chargeable service.


10.2.2 If You terminate this Agreement or cancel Your contract before the end of the agreed Subscription Term under a Purchase Order, You shall remain liable for all fees and charges due for the remainder of the Subscription Term, as specified in Your Purchase Order. Any outstanding balance through the date of termination, including the remainder of the contract price, shall immediately become due and payable in full. Such amounts are an early termination charge agreed in advance and are not a charge for switching or data retrieval.


10.2.3 Sections 1, 3, 5, 7.3, 7.7, 8 (to the extent not satisfied during the term of the Agreement), 10.2, 10.3, and 11 through 15 of this Agreement shall survive its expiration or termination for any reason.


10.3 Switching and Data Retrieval (EU Data Act). This Section 10.3 applies where You are established in the European Union and the Tenjin Platform constitutes a data processing service within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 (the “Data Act”), and prevails over any conflicting provision of this Agreement to the extent required by the Data Act.


10.3.1 You may at any time notify Tenjin in writing of Your decision to switch to another provider, to Your own infrastructure, or to erase Your data, with a notice period of no more than two (2) months. A downgrade to the free plan is not a switch under this Section 10.3. Following the notice period, a transitional period of up to thirty (30) calendar days applies during which Tenjin will provide reasonable assistance with the switching process, followed by a data retrieval period of at least thirty (30) calendar days.


10.3.2 During the retrieval period, You may retrieve all exportable data, being Your Data and the reports, metrics, and configuration data generated for Your account that are available through the Tenjin dashboard, the Tenjin APIs, the Aggregated Data Exporter, and any Data Export Feature included in Your Subscription, in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format. Data specific to the internal functioning of the Tenjin Platform, including Tenjin’s models, scoring logic, and Aggregate Data, is not exportable data.


10.3.3 Tenjin does not charge switching charges or data egress charges in connection with the switching process. Standard subscription fees remain payable until the effective date of termination, and early termination charges under Section 10.2.2 remain payable where applicable. After the retrieval period, or any longer period agreed with You, Your Data will be deleted in accordance with the Data Processing Addendum.


10.3.4 Information on the procedures for switching and on Tenjin’s data export interfaces and formats is available in the Documentation.


11. CONFIDENTIALITY


11.1 Obligations. Each of the parties agrees to maintain in confidence any information disclosed by either party to the other party, either directly or indirectly, in writing, orally or by inspection of tangible objects, which is designated as “Confidential,” “Proprietary” or some similar designation, or if given orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary within a reasonable time (not to exceed thirty (30) days) after the oral disclosure, or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of the disclosure (“Confidential Information”). Customer Credentials shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer without any further designation. The receiving party shall not (a) disclose, use, transmit, inform or make available to any third party any Confidential Information of the disclosing party, other than to (i) the receiving party’s employees who have a “need to know” for the receiving party to exercise its rights or perform its obligations hereunder and (ii) professional advisers, and actual or prospective investors, provided that such employees, investors, acquirers and professional advisers are bound by agreements or, in the case of professional advisers, ethical duties respecting such Confidential Information in accordance with the terms of this Section 11, or (b) use any Confidential Information of the other party except as a necessary part of performing its obligations under this Agreement or as otherwise permitted by this Agreement. Each party shall take all actions as are reasonably necessary and appropriate to preserve and protect the Confidential Information of the other party and such party’s respective rights therein, at all times exercising at least the same degree of care that it uses to protect its own Confidential Information of a similar nature, which shall be at least a reasonable degree of care. Fraud signals derived at the level of Marketing Channels, sub-publishers, and site or placement identifiers under Section 5.2.3(iv) are Confidential Information of Tenjin.


11.2 Exclusions. Confidential Information shall not include any information that is (i) already rightfully known to the receiving party at the time of the disclosure; (ii) publicly known at the time of the disclosure or becomes publicly known through no wrongful act or failure of the receiving party; (iii) subsequently disclosed to the receiving party on a non-confidential basis by a third party not having a confidential relationship with the other party hereto that rightfully acquired such information; (iv) communicated to a third party by the receiving party with the express written consent of the disclosing party; or (v) independently developed by the receiving party. A disclosure of Confidential Information that is legally compelled to be disclosed pursuant to a subpoena, summons, order or other judicial or governmental process shall not be considered a breach of this Agreement; provided the receiving party provides prompt notice of any such subpoena, order, or the like to the disclosing party so that the disclosing party will have the opportunity to obtain a protective order or otherwise oppose the disclosure.

14. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY


14.1 Consequential Damages Waiver. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHALL EITHER PARTY, OR ITS LICENSORS, BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES (INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF BUSINESS PROFITS, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, LOSS OF BUSINESS INFORMATION AND THE LIKE) ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THE USE AND/OR INABILITY TO USE THE TENJIN PLATFORM, ANY TENJIN TOOL, OR THIS AGREEMENT, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

These limitations are integral to the calculation of fees in connection with the license of the Tenjin Platform, and were either party to assume any further liability, such consideration would out of necessity be substantially increased.

15. MISCELLANEOUS


15.1 Notices. Tenjin may provide notifications, whether such notifications are required by law or are for marketing or other business related purposes, to You via email notice, written or hard copy notice, or through posting of such notice on the Tenjin Platform, as determined by Tenjin in its sole discretion. Tenjin is not responsible for any automatic filtering You or Your network provider may apply to email notifications Tenjin sends to the email address provided by You.


15.2 Platform Modifications. We may, without prior notice, change the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool; stop providing the Tenjin Platform, any Tenjin Tool, or features of the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool, to You or to users generally; or create usage limits for the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool.


15.3 Modifications to this Agreement. Tenjin may, in its sole discretion, modify or update this Agreement from time to time, and so You should review this page periodically. When Tenjin changes the Agreement in a material manner, Tenjin will update the ‘last updated’ date at the top of this page and notify You via email or an in-platform notification. Your continued use of the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool after such notification constitutes Your acceptance of the terms of the amended Agreement. If You do not agree to any of these terms or any future terms, do not use or access (or continue to access) the Tenjin Platform or any Tenjin Tool.

Tenjin and Your relationship is solely that of independent contractors, and this Agreement will not establish any partnership, joint venture, employment, franchise or agency between Tenjin and You. <i class="image-fit">

<span>
<strong>Chun-Kai Wang</strong><em>Co-founder & CEO at Kooapps</em>
</span></div><div class="slide__article-content"><p>Revenue is up 8x since we first used Tenjin a few years ago and paid UA spend is 30x so Tenjin has completely transformed our business. We love Tenjin!</p></div><div class="slide__article-action">
<a href="/blog/how-to-scale-your-indie-studio-to-a-major-publisher-a-kooapps-case-study/"  class="btn-link">

</a></div></div></div></div><div class="slide"><div class="slide__group"><div class="slide__content"><h4>How Mexico’s Top Mobile Publisher Boosted their Portfolio LTV by 35% – A HyperBeard Case Study</h4><p>HyperBeard is the largest mobile game developer and publisher in Mexico, with 210 Million+ downloads on AppStore and PlayStore. They specialize in cute casual idle games targeting a young, adult, female demographic.</p><ul><li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>20%</strong> Increase in ROAS</span></li><li style="font-weight: 400;" aria-level="1"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>35%</strong> Portfolio LTV (Cross-Promo) Uplift</span></li></ul></div><div class="slide__article"><div class="slide__article-author">
<i class="image-fit">
<img data-lazyloaded="1" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIxMTAiIGhlaWdodD0iMTEwIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTEwIDExMCI+PHJlY3Qgd2lkdGg9IjEwMCUiIGhlaWdodD0iMTAwJSIgc3R5bGU9ImZpbGw6dHJhbnNwYXJlbnQ7ZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5OiAwLjE7Ii8+PC9zdmc+" width="110" height="110" data-src="https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/hyperbeard-1.png" class="attachment-thumbnail size-thumbnail" alt="" decoding="async" data-srcset="https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/hyperbeard-1.png 110w, https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/hyperbeard-1-12x12.png 12w" data-sizes="(max-width: 110px) 100vw, 110px" />													</i>
<span>
<strong>Alex Kozachenko</strong><em>Co-founder & CEO at HyperBeard</em>
</span></div><div class="slide__article-content"><p>We love using DataVault. Historically, we were just using whatever was available on the dashboard with whatever MMP we were using. It’s great for creative performance tracking, and Portfolio LTV analysis.</p></div><div class="slide__article-action">

</a></div></div></div></div><div class="slide"><div class="slide__group"><div class="slide__content"><h4>Ad Revenue Callbacks and ROAS campaigns increased YOMI Studio’s ARPDAU by 60% – Case Study</h4><p>In this case study, we take you through the journey of YOMI Studio as they enter an unprecedented phase of hyper-growth after incorporating Tenjin’s Ad Revenue Callbacks and ROAS Campaigns. Here is a summary of what they achieved:</p><ul><li><strong>60</strong> Hours per Month of Co-founder’s Time Saved</li><li><strong>60%</strong> ARPDAU Uplift</li></ul></div><div class="slide__article"><div class="slide__article-author">
<i class="image-fit">
<img data-lazyloaded="1" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIxMTAiIGhlaWdodD0iMTEwIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTEwIDExMCI+PHJlY3Qgd2lkdGg9IjEwMCUiIGhlaWdodD0iMTAwJSIgc3R5bGU9ImZpbGw6dHJhbnNwYXJlbnQ7ZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5OiAwLjE7Ii8+PC9zdmc+" width="110" height="110" data-src="https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/avatar-1.png" class="attachment-thumbnail size-thumbnail" alt="" decoding="async" data-srcset="https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/avatar-1.png 110w, https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/avatar-1-12x12.png 12w" data-sizes="(max-width: 110px) 100vw, 110px" />													</i>
<span>
<strong>Light Nguyen</strong><em>Co-founder at YOMI Studio</em>
</span></div><div class="slide__article-content"><p>Combining Tenjin Ad Revenue Callbacks and ROAS campaigns has enabled us to spend less time on optimization but still scale campaigns at will, moving YOMI into an unprecedented phase of hyper-growth.</p></div><div class="slide__article-action">

</svg>
</i>
</a></div></div></div></div><div class="slide"><div class="slide__group"><div class="slide__content"><h4>How to increase ROAS and LTV for SKAN campaigns with TikTok & Tenjin – A Tokyo Tsushin Case Study</h4><p>Tokyo Tsushin partnered with TikTok and Tenjin to easily identify users who would trigger valuable in-app events such as purchase, subscribe, and level completion, while controlling costs.</p><ul><li><strong>33%</strong> Increase in Day 7 ROAS</li><li><strong>24%</strong> Íncrease in Day 3 LTV</li></ul></div><div class="slide__article"><div class="slide__article-author">
<i class="image-fit">
<img data-lazyloaded="1" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIxMTAiIGhlaWdodD0iMTEwIiB2aWV3Qm94PSIwIDAgMTEwIDExMCI+PHJlY3Qgd2lkdGg9IjEwMCUiIGhlaWdodD0iMTAwJSIgc3R5bGU9ImZpbGw6dHJhbnNwYXJlbnQ7ZmlsbC1vcGFjaXR5OiAwLjE7Ii8+PC9zdmc+" width="110" height="110" data-src="https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/avatar-1-1.png" class="attachment-thumbnail size-thumbnail" alt="" decoding="async" data-srcset="https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/avatar-1-1.png 110w, https://tenjin.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/avatar-1-1-12x12.png 12w" data-sizes="(max-width: 110px) 100vw, 110px" />													</i>
<span>
<strong>Kasuga Yachi</strong><em>Marketing Section Manager at Tokyo Tsushin</em>
</span></div><div class="slide__article-content"><p>Launching scalable SKAN campaigns is definitely a challenge. Thanks to the combination of TikTok and Tenjin, we were able to run goal-oriented SKAN campaigns at scale.</p></div><div class="slide__article-action">
